name: Linux TCP root
tile_line: Any IPv4 TCP server. Root shown only via MPTCP.
tldr: A race in the Linux kernel's IPv4 TCP handshake (4.4 or later) lets a remote attacker corrupt kernel memory, no login. Root was shown via MPTCP, but turning MPTCP off doesn't make you safe. No public exploit. Update and reboot.
summary: A race in the kernel's IPv4 TCP handshake code lets a remote attacker with no login corrupt kernel memory by sending connection requests that carry IP options. On 27 Oct, Anthropic showed remote root against a server with a Multipath TCP (MPTCP) listener, but the bug is in plain TCP, so turning off MPTCP doesn't make you safe. Full exploit code isn't public and no attacks are reported.

affected.label: Kernel 4.4 or later, not yet patched
affected.text: Upstream fixes: 5.10.272, 5.15.223, 6.1.190, 6.6.159, 6.12.113, 6.18.56, 7.2.10, 7.3. Distro kernels backport, so compare with your distro's fixed version under Update. RHEL 6 and 7 are not affected.

affected.label: Accepts IPv4 TCP connections
affected.text: Any IPv4 TCP listener counts, MPTCP or not: Red Hat says MPTCP is not required, and RHEL with MPTCP off by default is still affected. IPv6 is not affected by the main bug. Nearly every server has a TCP listener.

do.label: Update the kernel and reboot
do.text: Install your distro's fixed kernel (listed below), then reboot. Ubuntu 20.04 (5.4.0-247.267) and 18.04 (4.15.0-263.275) fixes are in Ubuntu Pro only. Debian 12's linux-6.12: 6.12.113-1~deb12u1. Cloud and HWE kernels have their own versions.

do.label: Can't reboot yet? Live patch or filter
do.text: RHEL 8, RHEL 9.8 EUS and some RHEL SAP streams have a kpatch live patch (19 Nov; plain RHEL 9 has none) that avoids the reboot. Otherwise drop inbound IPv4 TCP packets with IP options in an nftables input chain (normal TCP options are fine). That reduces exposure but isn't a fix: traffic between containers on the same host can skip it.
do.cmd: ip protocol tcp ip hdrlength > 5 counter drop

do.label: Optional: turn off MPTCP
do.text: Blocks the known root path only (the public demo used an MPTCP listener; Go 1.24+ programs open them by default). May break programs that need MPTCP. For Go services, `GODEBUG=multipathtcp=0` does the same per program. `sudo ss -Mlnp` lists MPTCP listeners.

slack: Linux TCP remote root (CVE-2026-98432): use-after-free race in IPv4 TCP handshake code, kernels 4.4+, triggerable remotely with no login via SYNs carrying IP options. Anthropic showed remote root on 27 Oct against an MPTCP listener, but any IPv4 TCP listener has the bug, so disabling MPTCP is not a fix. No full public exploit, no attacks, not in CISA KEV. Fix: patched distro kernel + reboot (Debian, Ubuntu 22.04+, RHEL 8–10 out; Ubuntu 20.04/18.04 via Ubuntu Pro; RHEL kpatch available). Stopgap: nftables drop of IPv4 TCP with IP options.
